### 1. Architecture Overview

Prometheus’s ingestion path funnels through the `storage.Appender` interface defined in `storage/interface.go` (see `Append` signature and related comment block at lines 269‑312). Any component that ingests new samples—local scrapers, remote-write receivers, OTLP translators, or Mimir distributors—obtains an `Appender` to batch their writes, optionally caching a `SeriesRef`, setting options (`SetOptions`), and appending float samples (`Append`) before committing or rolling back via `AppenderTransaction`. The `fanout` proxy layer (`storage/fanout.go`) mirrors this flow: when the fanout storage is used, it instantiates fanout appenders and fanout appenders for exemplars/histograms/series metadata, propagating each call to primary and secondary backends and squashing errors (see methods such as `SetOptions`, `Append`, `AppendExemplar`, `AppendHistogram`, `AppendSTZeroSample` and the V2 equivalents documented in the metadata summary). Backend implementations such as the TSDB head (`tsdb/head_append_v2.go`) supply concrete `AppenderV2` objects via `Head.AppenderV2`, while remote write receivers and OTLP translators rely on storage appenders exposed via the `storage.Storage` interface (e.g., `storage/remote/write.go`, `storage/remote/otlptranslator/.../metrics_to_prw.go`). Adding a `AppendCTZeroSample` method to `Appender` therefore requires updates in every layer that constructs or consumes these appenders to ensure zero samples for counter resets are handled transactionally across all ingestion paths.

### 2. Detailed Analysis

#### `storage/interface.go` – Core `Appender` contract
- Lines 269‑312 define `AppendOptions` and the `Appender` interface. Every ingestion path depends on this contract (scrapers, remote write, OTLP translation, Mimir distributors).
- The interface already exposes `Append(ref SeriesRef, labels.Labels, t int64, v float64)` and the auxiliary interfaces (ExemplarAppender, HistogramAppender, MetadataUpdater, StartTimestampAppender).
- The requested change is to add `AppendCTZeroSample(ref SeriesRef, l labels.Labels, t, ct int64) (SeriesRef, error)` so all implementers must support writing counter-timestamp zero samples. This method will sit alongside the existing appender methods (per lines 314‑329 for helper interfaces) and must be invoked by any feature that needs to append counter-reset zero samples.

#### `storage/fanout.go` – Fanout proxy implementing `Appender`
- The fanout storage wraps primary and secondaries and implements all `Appender` operations (`SetOptions`, `Append`, `AppendExemplar`, `AppendHistogram`, `AppendSTZeroSample`, `Commit`, `Rollback`) as well as the V2 equivalents (see section map entries around L126‑349 and function list in metadata). 
- Since the new method must be available wherever the `Appender` interface is implemented, `fanoutAppender` needs to forward `AppendCTZeroSample` to each underlying storage backend (primary+secondaries) while preserving the current error handling behavior (partial errors and squashing logic described near `Partial Error Handling (~L302-319)`).
- Because fanout already handles `AppendSTZeroSample` (see the function list), it provides a natural insertion point for the CT variant—ensuring the method is invoked in both V1 and V2 appenders.

#### `tsdb/head_append_v2.go` – TSDB head appender implementation
- The `headAppenderV2` struct (lines 106‑219 per section map) is the canonical ingestion path within the TSDB head. It already handles float/histogram appends, exemplars (`Append` and `appendExemplars`), and best-effort ST zero samples (`bestEffortAppendSTZeroSample`). 
- Adding `AppendCTZeroSample` would require wiring it into this file so that the head can materialize counter-reset zero samples during ingestion, similar to how `bestEffortAppendSTZeroSample` is described (“Appends zero sample for ST timestamp with counter reset hint”).
- This ensures counter-timestamp zero samples appear in WAL/appender flows and gives concrete behavior when the new method is invoked by higher-level components (scrapers, remote write) that depend on `Appender`.

#### Remote write & OTLP ingestion paths (implied)
- Remote write storage (`storage/remote/write.go`) exposes `storage.Storage` with `Appender` creation methods (metadata shows it exposes `Appender`, `AppenderV2`, etc.). Any change to the base `Appender` interface implies these constructors must provide appenders that implement the new method before returning. 
- The OTLP‑to‑Prometheus translator (`storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/metrics_to_prw.go`) translates OTLP metrics to Prometheus samples and uses the storage appender to submit data (per file purpose). It must be aware of the new method so counter resets derived from OTLP input can be forwarded as CT zero samples, mirroring the existing sample append flow.

#### Appender consumers
- Scrape loops (`scrape/scrape_append_v2.go`) rely on `Appender` to ingest scraped data (per file purpose). They will need to call the new `AppendCTZeroSample` when enforcing counter-timestamp zero-sample logic, ensuring scraped counter resets get recorded precisely.
- Scrape manager/target utilities (`scrape/target.go`) control append behavior (limiting sample count/time bounds) and might need to adapt metadata (since they already monitor appender limits per purpose). The new method likely propagates through these files unless handled elsewhere.

### 3. Relevant Files

Must forward `AppendCTZeroSample` to primary/secondary backends, maintaining current partial-error handling and synchronous behavior described around `fanoutAppender` and `fanoutAppenderV2`. |

Needs to implement the new method to persist CT zero samples at the head level; references include `headAppenderV2.Append`, `append*` helpers, and `bestEffortAppendSTZeroSample`. |

| prometheus | `scrape/scrape_append_v2.go` | Scraper loops append samples to storage appenders; needs to invoke the new method to ensure scraped counter resets produce CT zero samples before calling `Commit`. |
| prometheus | `scrape/target.go` | Manages scrape targets and limits appender behavior per purpose summary (including sample count/time). Updates may be required to propagate CT zero samples (as part of append behavior enforcement). |

| prometheus | `storage/remote/metadata_watcher.go` | Uses `MetadataAppender` to push metadata to remote writes (per purpose). If metadata flows relate to counter resets, ensure the new method is handled when metadata updates trigger zero samples. |

| prometheus | `util/teststorage/appender_test.go` | Tests that exercise appenders need to cover the new method to ensure the mock and expected behavior align. |

**Note:** All files above are specifically referenced via tool outputs (metadata and content sections) that describe their purposes and interactions with the `Appender` interface. The new method requires coordinated updates across ingestion paths (scrapers, remote write, OTLP translation, fanout, TSDB head, mocks, and metadata watchers) to preserve the contract’s invariants and ensure counter-timestamp zero samples are handled uniformly.
